statement: Hero's transmitted description specifies steam-driven rotation of a sphere but no productive load or output measurement.

sources.supports: Mechanism and editorial framing of the inspected edition.

counterevidence: A text's omission does not establish absence of experiments elsewhere.
inference_limits: Description is not proof of ancient deployment, first invention, or prevalence.

test.reason: Bounded statement about what the inspected passage says and omits.

statement: Roby offers a philosophical reading of Hero's sphere as an alternative to judging it as an unsuccessful industrial engine; original purpose remains contested.

sources.supports: Critique of teleology and discussion of Keyser's philosophical interpretation.

counterevidence: Other Heronian devices have practical applications; the corpus permits several uses.
inference_limits: The original Keyser paper and full Roby monograph were not read.

test.mechanism_chain: A demonstration aimed at analysing motion -> a text specifies visible rotation -> no productive load is needed for that purpose.
test.strongest_rival: A practical experimental device may omit applications or have had lost uses.
test.discriminating_observation: Ancient user testimony or a connected working apparatus associated with a specified purpose.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S01 passage and ANC-S02 introductory interpretation; no user account found.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Both purposes can predict the same surviving description.

statement: The inspected Hero sources do not establish sustained productive operation or commercial cost competitiveness of the rotating sphere.

sources.supports: No load, duration or cost record.
Warns against reading modern industrial goals into the device.

counterevidence: A reconstruction could show useful work, but would not itself establish ancient commercial adoption.
inference_limits: This is a boundary of this source set, not a claim that such operation was physically impossible.

test.reason: Evidence-scope statement; no causal claim explaining ancient non-adoption.

statement: Barbegal's sixteen-wheel installation and carbonate traces establish productive hydraulic machinery and repeated operation at a particular Roman site.

sources.supports: Site configuration and operational deposits.
Configuration and terminal operation of selected structures.

counterevidence: The sixteen wooden wheels do not survive; reconstruction combines architecture and casts.
inference_limits: No empire-wide adoption share, exact annual output, or purchaser identity follows.

test.reason: Site-level deployment evidence, not a diffusion or causal estimate.

statement: Barbegal's repeated seasonal interruptions support a variable operating schedule; ship's biscuit production is a plausible but unconfirmed market explanation.

sources.locator: Results: Stable isotope composition, Fig. 4; Discussion
sources.supports: Truncated seasonal sequences and the authors' hardtack interpretation.

counterevidence: Water availability, other seasonal markets, or other operating choices might also produce pauses.
inference_limits: The carbonate records do not identify the product's final consumer.

test.mechanism_chain: Seasonal shipping demand -> mill managers schedule production -> recurrent late-summer/autumn pauses.
test.strongest_rival: Seasonal water limits or a different flour market could cause the same schedule.
test.discriminating_observation: Independent seasonal water reconstruction plus securely associated baking, storage, shipment or purchasing records.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S03 isotope results and alternative-market discussion inspected; no direct customer record.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Production purpose is inferred from timing and location; alternatives not eliminated.

statement: Three western Barbegal flumes indicate staged terminal operation while aqueduct water continued; loss of water supply alone does not explain that observed sequence.

sources.locator: §5 discussion of flumes A–C, Fig. 9; §6 Conclusions, pp. 604–607
sources.supports: Different terminal sequences and continued water flow.

counterevidence: Continuing flow need not mean unchanged discharge or a fully adequate supply.
inference_limits: Neither the entire site's chronology nor a unique cause of abandonment is identified.

test.mechanism_chain: Equipment deterioration or changing use -> uneven withdrawal/alteration of machinery -> individual mills cease while water remains.
test.strongest_rival: Declining discharge could impair mills unevenly even without a complete cutoff.
test.discriminating_observation: Synchronous flow-rate and component histories across both trains, independently dated demand and repair evidence.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S04 flume microstratigraphy and conclusions; supply did not simply cease everywhere first.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Demand, materials, water quantity and organisational capacity remain entangled.

statement: Roman productive waterpower and enslaved hydraulic maintenance contradict an absolute incompatibility between slavery and complex machinery; the effect of labour costs on marginal adoption remains unidentified.

sources.supports: Productive watermill installation in the Roman period.
Enslaved workers in a sophisticated hydraulic service.

counterevidence: Neither source identifies Barbegal workers' legal status or a comparison of machine and labour prices.
inference_limits: Rejects an absolute proposition only; it does not estimate a slavery effect or deny coercion.

test.mechanism_chain: An absolute institutional prohibition predicts no productive machinery within the slaveholding Roman setting -> Barbegal is a counterexample.
test.strongest_rival: Slavery reduces adoption incentives for some tasks without prohibiting all machinery.
test.discriminating_observation: Task-matched adoption and ownership/cost evidence could test the conditional claim; no such series is available here.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S03 operating machinery and ANC-S05 enslaved maintenance arrangements found.
test.remaining_ambiguity: The universal version fails; the conditional economic proposition remains open.

statement: Frontinus reports about 240 publicly owned and 460 imperial enslaved aqueduct workers organised into specialised maintenance functions.

sources.supports: Reported headcounts, ownership and functions.

counterevidence: His account also complains about diversion of workers to private tasks.
inference_limits: High confidence in the reported arrangement, not an independently verified staffing census.

test.reason: Attribution to a specific ancient account, with performance limits explicit.

statement: Frontinus describes recurrent funding and timed, sequential shutdowns as arrangements for maintaining Rome's aqueduct service.

sources.supports: Treasury/imperial funding, advance preparation and shutdown procedures.

counterevidence: Prescriptions may respond to poor compliance; funds and personnel alone do not guarantee repair quality.
inference_limits: No causal estimate of improved reliability or fiscal adequacy.

test.mechanism_chain: Funding and advance scheduling -> personnel/materials available during limited shutdowns -> intended preservation of supply.
test.strongest_rival: Actual reliability may have depended more on redundant routes and favourable water sources, with rules poorly observed.
test.discriminating_observation: Work records or dated repairs showing compliance and service changes before/after procedural changes.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S05 prescriptive and financial passages inspected; no independent operational audit found.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Administrative intention cannot be equated with realised performance.

statement: Bannon's evidence distinguishes civic aqueduct grants from other water rights and shows roles for local control, payment and status; infrastructure did not imply a single empire-wide administration or equal access.

sources.supports: Distinct rights configurations and social/political dimensions.

counterevidence: Open-access fountains also existed; elite grants do not imply universal exclusion.
inference_limits: Rules and examples cannot quantify household supply or the distribution of actual consumption.

test.reason: Describes institutional distinctions in the inspected legal-historical analysis.

statement: Procopius reports aqueduct disruption stopping Rome's mills in 537, fodder scarcity limiting animal substitution, and Tiber boatmills restoring grinding while wells still supplied drinking water.

sources.supports: Reported sequence, constraint and alternative services.

counterevidence: Narrative may magnify the general's resourcefulness and adequacy of replacement capacity.
inference_limits: No throughput, household coverage or proof of permanent aqueduct abandonment.

test.mechanism_chain: Siege cuts aqueduct flow and limits fodder -> existing mills and animal alternatives are constrained -> river-driven boatmills substitute for grinding.
test.strongest_rival: Some milling may have continued elsewhere; the emergency innovation may be less comprehensive than the narrative claims.
test.discriminating_observation: Contemporary grain/mill records and securely dated traces of competing installations during the siege.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S07 explicitly links disruption, feed scarcity and boatmills; drinking water has other sources.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Detailed sequence is one literary witness and cannot quantify city-wide adequacy.

statement: Excavated early Arabian galleries complicate a single Iranian origin narrative; Boucharlat's polycentric account remains a hypothesis under uneven dating and disputed water-source identifications.

sources.supports: Regional evidence, disputed classifications and chronological limits.

counterevidence: Poor excavation and dating in Iran can produce an apparent geographical priority.
inference_limits: Earliest known evidence is not first invention; resemblance is not transmission.

test.mechanism_chain: Different local groundwater conditions -> locally adjusted gallery construction -> similar broad forms without necessary common origin.
test.strongest_rival: Diffusion followed by adaptation could generate the same variation.
test.discriminating_observation: Secure construction dates and distinctive shared techniques across plausible intermediate sites.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S08 regional evidence inspected; no complete transmission chain established.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Non-observation in Iran is especially weak where survey and dating are incomplete.

statement: The al-Madam sequence of deepening and later silting is consistent with declining water availability followed by discontinued maintenance, but does not isolate environmental change from settlement reorganisation.

sources.supports: Deepening, diminished flow interpretation and abandonment.

counterevidence: Reduced cleaning or changed settlement could itself increase silting and apparent hydraulic failure.
inference_limits: Underlying excavation sequence is mediated through a synthesis; regional climatic causation is not identified.

test.mechanism_chain: Lower water availability -> deepen gallery -> diminishing returns or disrupted upkeep -> abandonment.
test.strongest_rival: Political or economic relocation reduces maintenance first; silting follows.
test.discriminating_observation: Independent water-table indicators temporally preceding deepening, versus evidence of prior settlement/maintenance withdrawal.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S08 alteration and sediment sequence found; no independent local time series inspected.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Water and maintenance can change reciprocally; climatic attribution is underdetermined.

statement: Polybius reports that earlier Persian rulers offered five generations of cultivation rights for bringing water to unirrigated land; the inspected translation does not explicitly state a tax exemption.

sources.supports: Reported incentive and expense in Paton's wording.
Critical contextualisation of the reported galleries.

counterevidence: Other translations or legal interpretations may construe the benefit differently.
inference_limits: Local retrospective testimony is not an actual grant deed or proof of universal enforcement.

test.reason: Exact attribution to a transmitted report and its inspected translation; investment causation is separately hypothetical.

statement: A gravity-fed groundwater gallery can supply its outlet only when water is available at a compatible elevation and the channel remains passable; knowing the technique alone does not establish local feasibility.

sources.supports: Geometry of gallery supply and locally adjusted depth.

counterevidence: Pumped or surface-fed supply can replace the service, but constitutes a different configuration.
inference_limits: Physical constraint, not a historical cost model or estimate of aquifer sustainability.

test.mechanism_chain: Accessible groundwater and gradient -> gravity flow through a passable gallery -> outlet supply.
test.strongest_rival: An apparently similar tunnel may instead convey an external surface source.
test.discriminating_observation: Trace the collecting section, outlet elevations and water source; distinguish groundwater interception from conveyance.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S08 explicitly separates gallery types and water sources.
test.remaining_ambiguity: The physical relationship is clear; source classification of particular early galleries remains disputed.

statement: Peng's presentation of inscriptions dated 168 and 199 CE supports official involvement in Dujiangyan's late Han maintenance; his interpretation relates the work to organised labour obligations.

sources.locator: §1 Early repair in archaeological materials; §4 Labour organisation
sources.supports: Inscription readings and labour interpretation.

counterevidence: Commemorative inscriptions may selectively praise officials; labour status is partly inferred.
inference_limits: Reproduction inspected, not original rubbings; no household burden or consent measure.

test.reason: Reports bounded attestations and an attributed interpretation, without estimating their effect on longevity.

statement: Extending Dujiangyan's regular repair system back to its Qin foundation is an inference; the date of the six-character maintenance rule remains disputed in the inspected scholarship.

sources.locator: §1 opening discussion; §2 competing dates of the six-character rule
sources.supports: Explicit evidentiary reservation and competing chronological attributions.

counterevidence: The engineering need for periodic work and Qin waterwork legislation make early maintenance plausible.
inference_limits: Need for repairs does not establish an identical institution or uninterrupted service.

test.mechanism_chain: Sediment-prone headworks -> repeated early repairs -> institutionalised routine by the foundation period.
test.strongest_rival: Formalisation occurred later, with retrospective attribution to Li Bing.
test.discriminating_observation: Contemporary Qin repair instructions or securely dated work episodes rather than later retrospective attribution.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S10 acknowledges missing decisive early evidence and reports disputed dates.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Functional plausibility cannot determine institutional chronology.

statement: Zheng et al.'s model links Dujiangyan's geometry and flow regimes to sediment diversion and identifies dredging needs, but cannot demonstrate unchanged ancient geometry or uninterrupted operation.

sources.supports: Modelled mechanisms, maintenance requirement, modern alterations and limits.

counterevidence: The authors themselves call for more comprehensive model validation; contemporary works modify flows.
inference_limits: Numerical experiment is not an ancient performance series or a causal explanation of two millennia.

test.mechanism_chain: Specified geometry and inflow -> flow and sediment partition -> irrigation intake protected, with residual sediment requiring dredging.
test.strongest_rival: Different historic geometry, unmodelled regulation or alternative sediment parameters may produce different outcomes.
test.discriminating_observation: Validate against measured flows and sediment, then test independently reconstructed historic configurations and repair records.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S11 model, modern-dam exclusion and validation caveat inspected.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Physical plausibility in model conditions does not identify historical persistence.

statement: Dholavira's excavated water system combined storage, diversion and drainage; the ICOMOS phase narrative locates major reservoirs in an expansion episode rather than one timeless configuration.

sources.supports: Structures and staged construction.
Existing reservoirs distinguish excavated evidence from new GPR hypotheses.

counterevidence: Detailed construction chronology requires the excavation archive; some proposed structures remain unexcavated.
inference_limits: Does not establish precise population served, ownership or water reliability.

test.reason: Material configuration and attributed phasing, not identification of a cause of urban growth.

statement: The Dholavira GPR study proposes reservoirs or bunds and possible flood damage, explicitly requiring excavation to confirm those interpretations.

sources.locator: Archaeological interpretations and Conclusion, pp. 884–886; Fig. 9
sources.supports: Alternative feature identifications and explicit excavation requirement.

counterevidence: Similar reflections and rubble can have different structural or depositional explanations.
inference_limits: No dated ancient flood or causal link to city-wide decline is established.

test.mechanism_chain: Flood damages water-control walls -> walls disappear and rubble accumulates -> particular radar signature.
test.strongest_rival: Other collapse, dismantling or fill processes could create comparable reflections.
test.discriminating_observation: Excavated structural relationships, dated flood sediments and identifiable displaced masonry.
test.evidence_sought_found: ANC-S12 reports geophysical features and alternative interpretations, not excavation confirmation.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Radar does not directly determine function, age or destruction mechanism.

statement: ICOMOS reports unrestored water-structure damage and occupation gaps at Dholavira; this limits a narrative of continuous urban service but does not identify the cause of declining use.

sources.locator: Description and history, Stages V–VII, printed p. 15
sources.supports: Unrestored damage, contraction and gaps in the phase narrative.

counterevidence: A service may continue at reduced scale, and alternative water arrangements may leave little evidence.
inference_limits: No warranted inference that water failure caused rather than followed settlement change.

test.reason: Attributes phased observations without converting association into a causal explanation.

statement: These cases show why cessation of an installation, substitution of its service, and loss of technical knowledge must be tested separately; survival of a named system likewise does not establish unchanged operation.

sources.supports: Staged local cessation.
Reported service substitution.
Adaptation and abandonment.
Chronological uncertainty in maintenance.
Changing settlement/service context.

counterevidence: Some episodes may genuinely include skill loss; archaeological disappearance can also coincide with institutional collapse.
inference_limits: Purposive cases do not estimate the frequency of any mechanism or demonstrate universal continuity.

test.mechanism_chain: Loss or change of a local complement -> installation ceases or service relocates -> material disappearance without necessary erasure of know-how.
test.strongest_rival: Skilled communities or transmission may themselves disappear, causing installation failure.
test.discriminating_observation: Trace practitioners, texts and equivalent working installations alongside independently dated service cessation.
test.evidence_sought_found: Selected ANC cases contain differing terminal sequences and alternatives; no complete knowledge-transmission series was assembled.
test.remaining_ambiguity: Material and knowledge losses may reinforce each other; bounded alternatives disprove inevitability, not all loss.
